box: Box B -- love-match's central claim: (a,b) and (b,a) are the same reading. Proved in the live page for two different pairs, each in both orders, reloading between each order to rule out any in-memory-only agreement.
method: scripts/driver.mjs, one CDP tab per script run against the same served build as Box A. For pair 1 (ก้อง / ฟ้า): wiped storage on-origin, added both names via #roster-add-name/#roster-add-btn (auto-checked), clicked #start-round (waited 400ms for the async mount listener), picked ก้อง then ฟ้า by exact chip textContent, read the result. Then navigated (full reload, same tab) back to /game/love-match/ and verified the reload lands on the SETUP panel, not a resumed round (love-match saves no mid-round checkpoint by design, and the module's own comment says so -- checked rather than assumed, via #player-setup.hidden === false and an empty #stage). The last-used group was pre-ticked automatically after reload (roster survives in localStorage) -- verified via the checked checkbox labels before proceeding, without re-adding names. Clicked #start-round again and picked ฟ้า then ก้อง (order reversed). The pair paragraph (identified by its unique '1.25rem' inline-style substring) is the positive control that order really was reversed: it read 'ก้อง กับ ฟ้า' first and 'ฟ้า กับ ก้อง' second -- if both had printed the same string, the swap would not have been proven. Repeated the whole sequence for a second, unrelated pair (ตูน / แนน) after a fresh on-origin wipe.
